question: Holding both the matched pair and species identity fixed, does increasing rainfall contrast preferentially reactivate full choruses at physical sites that the same species used in earlier years?
population: Physically stable matched pairs. Candidate species must have been detected in the same State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum strictly before the earlier year of the pair and must be absent from the focal dry route.
cell_unit: Candidate species x one of the ten physical SiteIDs in the wet run.
exposure: prior_same_site=1 if the same species was detected at that SiteID in an eligible run strictly before the earlier survey year, else 0.

fixed_effect_design.eligibility: Group must contain both prior_same_site=1 and prior_same_site=0 cells.
fixed_effect_design.transformation: Demean outcome, prior_same_site and prior_same_site*rain_contrast within pair x species.
fixed_effect_design.model: demeaned outcome ~ demeaned prior_same_site + demeaned(prior_same_site*rain_contrast), no intercept.
fixed_effect_design.interpretation: The interaction coefficient compares sites for the same species in the same matched comparison, removing all pair-level conditions and species-level propensity.

primary_prediction: Coefficient on demeaned(prior_same_site*rain_contrast) >0 with complete 95% CI >0.
gate: >=500 informative pair x species groups, >=5000 cells and >=200 routes.
sensitivity: Repeat on same-observer pairs; gate >=350 groups, >=3500 cells and >=150 routes.
interpretation: Support is direct evidence of rainfall-dependent reactivation of previously used species-site combinations, independent of species identity and pair-level conditions.
The analysis still does not identify individual frogs, continuous occupancy, reproductive success, or the proximal physiological trigger.
No causal rainfall claim is authorized.
